parameters.definition: Qualitative CFD comparison of 280 and 580 bar cases.

process_relations.target_process: mass injection rate and fuel-air mixing
process_relations.notes: Paper attributes faster combustion and improved oxidation to injection-rate/mixing changes.
Engine and CFD evidence are combined in the conclusion.

mechanism_relations.notes: Mechanistic link is supported by reacting-CFD comparison.
Outcome is load-dependent and accompanied by noise/NOx tradeoffs.

evidence_candidates.claim: Increasing natural-gas rail pressure shortened the mixing-controlled combustion event in the tested HPDI engine, with the strongest benefits at high-load/high-speed conditions.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: The 300-to-600 bar program and CFD comparison associate higher pressure with increased injection rate and improved late-cycle mixing.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Single engine architecture; transient-cycle performance was not evaluated.
evidence_candidates.potential_chapter_role: HPDI injection-pressure control and mixing-rate mechanism.

evidence_candidates.claim: The efficiency and PM advantages of higher gas pressure came with higher combustion harshness and NOx, and nozzle-flow control was proposed as mitigation.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Conclusion reports load-dependent efficiency/PM benefits plus combustion-noise and NOx penalties.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Tradeoffs depend on operating point and nozzle design.

key_results: Cycle-composite efficiency benefit was of order 3% and PM reduction 40–60%; peak-torque alternatives were reported as 7% efficiency, 20% power, or 90% PM benefit.
Benefits were concentrated above roughly 75% load.
mechanisms: Higher pressure raises gas mass injection rate and improves late-cycle mixing/oxidation; it also raises heat-release intensity.
extraction_notes: Tier 2 targeted extraction; figure curves were not digitized.

note_fields.Research Question: How does raising HPDI natural-gas injection pressure from conventional values to about 600 bar affect combustion, efficiency, and emissions?
note_fields.Study Type and Configuration: Heavy-duty pilot-ignited direct-injection natural-gas engine tests with injector modelling and reacting CFD.
note_fields.Geometry and Operating Conditions: Engine operating points span speed and load; benefits were concentrated at high load and high speed.
note_fields.Injection / Ambient Conditions: Natural-gas pressure was increased from about 300 to 600 bar; pressure reference type was not stated in the cited conclusion.
note_fields.Main Physical Observations: Higher pressure accelerated combustion and improved late-cycle mixing, while increasing harshness and NOx.
note_fields.Quantitative Results: Cycle-composite efficiency benefit about 3% and PM reduction 40–60%; peak-torque trade-space outcomes reported up to 7% efficiency, 20% power, or 90% PM benefit.
note_fields.Mechanism Proposed by Authors: Higher mass injection rate and subsequent enhanced mixing improve oxidation and fuel conversion.
note_fields.Limitations: Transient cycles were not tested; benefits depend on load, nozzle flow, EGR, and peak-cylinder-pressure constraints.
note_fields.Relevance to Review Mainline: Direct evidence connecting gas-rail pressure, underexpanded-jet mixing control, combustion phasing, and engine outcomes.

papers.tier1_role: Chapter-core counterexample on interacting HPDI jets and soot.
papers.study_context: Single-cylinder engine experiments with reacting CFD comparing paired-hole and single-hole injectors.

cases.description: Reference single-hole versus four paired-hole nozzle geometries.

source_locators.notes: Design intent and counterintuitive emission result.

Main gaseous fuel in pilot-ignited HPDI.

parameters.reported_value: seven single holes replaced by seven closely aligned hole pairs
parameters.definition: Paired-hole nozzle concept relative to equally spaced reference holes.
Natural-gas-basis local equivalence-ratio interval used as the soot-forming zone in the CFD analysis.
parameters.notes: Operational definition from the paper; not universalized.

process_relations.target_process: early air entrainment at equal penetration
process_relations.notes: The design achieved its immediate entrainment objective.

process_relations.source_process: paired-jet partial mixing and slower penetration
process_relations.target_process: fuel residence in soot-forming equivalence-ratio range
process_relations.notes: Used to explain increased PM despite enhanced entrainment.

mechanism_relations.notes: Mechanism reconciles increased entrainment with increased PM.

evidence_candidates.claim: Pairing nearby HPDI gas holes increased early air entrainment at equal penetration but did not reduce engine-out PM.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Reacting CFD resolved greater entrainment while engine measurements showed substantially higher PM.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Specific paired geometries and engine operating range.

evidence_candidates.claim: The authors attributed the PM increase to longer residence of natural gas in rich, moderate-temperature soot-forming conditions created by the merging jets.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: CFD mixture-fraction histories showed more fuel in the paper-defined 2<phi_g<6 interval.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Soot mechanism is inferred from mixture-state residence rather than directly resolved particulate chemistry.
evidence_candidates.potential_chapter_role: Jet-interaction topology and soot residence-time mechanism.

key_results: Paired-hole nozzles raised nonvolatile PM by factors of 3–10 and also raised CO.
Soot aggregate size and particle number increased, while primary particle size changed little.
mechanisms: Merging jets entrain air but create larger partially mixed volumes and prolonged residence in soot-forming conditions.
extraction_notes: Tier 2 targeted extraction; no particle-size distributions digitized.

note_fields.Research Question: Can closely paired gas holes reduce HPDI soot by enhancing jet interaction and air entrainment?
note_fields.Study Type and Configuration: Single-cylinder research engine comparison of a seven-hole reference with seven paired-hole arrangements, supported by reacting CFD.
note_fields.Main Physical Observations: The paired-hole concept increased early entrainment but raised CO and PM rather than lowering them.
note_fields.Quantitative Results: Nonvolatile PM was 3–10 times the reference across tested paired geometries.
note_fields.Mechanism Proposed by Authors: Merging/slower jets prolonged residence in rich moderate-temperature conditions conducive to soot formation.
note_fields.Mixing / Ignition / Combustion Consequen: When gas preceded the pilot sufficiently to premix broadly, the sensitivity to local jet geometry and PM difference largely vanished.
note_fields.Limitations: Results are geometry- and operating-range-specific; soot chemistry was interpreted through mixture-state residence.
note_fields.Relevance to Review Mainline: Important counterexample showing that more entrainment does not guarantee lower soot when interaction changes residence history.

papers.tier1_role: Chapter-core optical evidence on ambient state and pilot/gas interaction.
papers.study_context: Rapid-compression-machine optical study using schlieren/chemiluminescence and heat-release analysis.

cases.description: Four TDC pressure-temperature operating points with varied spatial and temporal pilot/gas overlap.

source_locators.notes: Fixed injection settings and four TDC states.
Ignition and combustion findings and transfer limitations.

parameters.definition: Diesel pilot injection pressure.
Natural-gas injection pressure.
Chamber pressure at TDC for OP1–OP4.
Adiabatic-core temperature at TDC for OP1–OP4.

process_relations.source_process: greater pilot/gas spatial overlap at low ambient reactivity
process_relations.notes: Ignition shifted downstream and could misfire when free path fell below lift-off length.
Same degree of premixing produced similar heat release across elevated states.

mechanism_relations.target_node: pilot chemical ignition delay and overlap sensitivity
mechanism_relations.notes: Low reactivity gives adjacent gas more time to disturb pilot mixture formation.

mechanism_relations.source_node: gas ignition timing relative to gas SOI
mechanism_relations.notes: Used as a cross-condition organizing variable.

evidence_candidates.claim: At lower chamber temperature and pressure, longer pilot ignition delay made pilot ignition more vulnerable to disruption by the adjacent natural-gas jet.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Optical imaging showed delayed/downstream pilot ignition and misfire when overlap reduced the free path below lift-off length.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Single free-jet arrangement without wall, swirl, or neighboring-jet effects.

evidence_candidates.claim: Relative pilot/gas timing controlled premixing and the resulting natural-gas heat-release mode across the tested elevated chamber states.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Heat-release behavior organized by gas ignition time relative to gas SOI, with timing controlling premixing.
evidence_candidates.limitations: RCM abstraction limits direct full-engine transfer.

key_results: TDC states were 75–125 bar and 780–920 K with fixed 2000 bar diesel and 330 bar gas injection.
Gas-jet soot luminosity generally began only after peak heat release; ending injection before that peak could prevent visible sooting.
mechanisms: Ambient reactivity controls pilot ignition delay; geometry and timing then determine whether gas disrupts or couples to the pilot.
extraction_notes: Tier 2 targeted extraction; optical intensities were not digitized.

note_fields.Research Question: How do ambient state, pilot/gas geometry, and relative timing govern pilot ignition and partially premixed HPDI combustion?
note_fields.Study Type and Configuration: Optical rapid-compression-machine experiment with a single diesel-pilot/natural-gas jet pair.
note_fields.Injection / Ambient Conditions: Diesel 2000 bar, gas 330 bar; four TDC states span 75–125 bar and 780–920 K.
note_fields.Main Physical Observations: Low ambient reactivity increased pilot sensitivity to gas-jet disturbance; timing controlled gas premixing.
note_fields.Mechanism Proposed by Authors: Chemical ignition delay sets the time available for jet interaction, while free path relative to lift-off length governs pilot survival.
note_fields.Limitations: No wall impingement, swirl, or multiple jets; application transfer is therefore conditional.
note_fields.Relevance to Review Mainline: Links ambient thermodynamic state and interaction timing to pilot robustness, premixing, HRR, and soot onset.

papers.tier1_role: Chapter-core conceptual model for pilot-ignited direct-injection NG combustion.
papers.study_context: Optically accessible 2-L single-cylinder engine with HRR and OH* chemiluminescence.

cases.description: Sweeps of NG injection pressure, gas pulse width, and relative injection timing.

parameters.definition: Optical single-cylinder engine experiment.
Research engine used for parametric sweep.

parameters.reported_value: non-premixed to distributed partially premixed to stratified premixed flame propagation as RIT decreased
parameters.definition: Observed primary NG combustion-mode transition with relative injection timing.

parameters.reported_value: along the side of the natural-gas jet
parameters.definition: Observed NG ignition location relative to jet structure.
parameters.notes: Contrasts with a previously published conceptualization.

process_relations.target_process: NG premixing and primary combustion mode
process_relations.notes: Dominant control compared with injection pressure for ignition.
Ignition remained comparatively insensitive to pressure.

mechanism_relations.notes: Transition spans non-premixed to flame-propagation regimes.
Separates ignition control from later mixing control.

evidence_candidates.claim: Relative pilot/gas injection timing was the primary control on natural-gas premixing and shifted combustion from non-premixed through distributed partially premixed to stratified premixed flame propagation.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: OH* reaction-zone analysis and HRR jointly resolved the regime transition.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Optical engine had low compression ratio, cylindrical bowl, and line-of-sight imaging.
evidence_candidates.potential_chapter_role: Conceptual staging of HPDI ignition and combustion.

evidence_candidates.claim: Natural-gas ignition was relatively insensitive to injection pressure, whereas higher pressure increased mixing-controlled heat release after ignition.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: The parametric sweep separates the ignition stage from subsequent non-premixed mixing control.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Results are bounded by the optical engine configuration.
evidence_candidates.potential_chapter_role: Stage-dependent role of gas injection pressure.

key_results: Five combustion processes were identified: pilot autoignition, NG ignition, rapid distributed partially premixed combustion, non-premixed combustion, and late-cycle oxidation.
mechanisms: RIT controls pre-ignition mixing; injection pressure primarily alters mixing after ignition.
extraction_notes: Tier 2 targeted extraction; no OH* intensity digitization.

note_fields.Research Question: Which distinct processes compose a typical pilot-ignited direct-injection NG event, and how do injection parameters affect them?
note_fields.Study Type and Configuration: Optically accessible 2-L single-cylinder engine using HRR and OH* chemiluminescence.
note_fields.Main Physical Observations: Five stages were identified; RIT dominated ignition/premixing while pressure affected later mixing-controlled combustion.
note_fields.Mechanism Proposed by Authors: NG ignites along the jet side, penetrates toward the bowl wall before ignition, and transitions among combustion regimes as premixing changes.
note_fields.Limitations: Low optical-engine compression ratio, cylindrical bowl, and line-of-sight imaging.
note_fields.Relevance to Review Mainline: Provides the project’s clearest process-resolved conceptual model for HPDI combustion.

papers.tier1_role: Chapter-core numerical evidence on pilot trigger, temperature, and radical effects.
papers.study_context: Engine-scale CFD plus homogeneous-reactor analysis at a medium-speed/load HPDI condition.

cases.description: Pilot+NG versus NG-only CFD and HRM sensitivity study.

parameters.reported_value: engine-like HPDI at 1400 RPM and 1285 Nm
parameters.definition: Selected medium-speed, medium-load operating point.
Main natural-gas injection pressure.
Estimated natural-gas temperature at injector nozzle.

parameters.reported_value: NG ignition within considered engine timing required initial temperature above approximately 1110 K in HRM
parameters.definition: Homogeneous-reactor ignition threshold under the selected engine-like composition/timing window.
parameters.notes: Not a universal methane ignition temperature.

process_relations.notes: NG-only CFD did not ignite at the selected condition.
Temperature dominates above 1100 K; radicals matter in an intermediate temperature band.

mechanism_relations.notes: Pilot trigger is necessary for the simulated operating point.
Only conditional within HRM state range.

evidence_candidates.claim: At the simulated medium-load HPDI point, the natural-gas injection did not ignite without the diesel pilot, demonstrating a required pilot trigger for that condition.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Paired CFD cases differed only by pilot injection; the NG-only case released no heat.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Single operating point and model-dependent chemistry/turbulence representation.
evidence_candidates.potential_chapter_role: Numerical isolation of the pilot-trigger function.

evidence_candidates.claim: In the homogeneous-reactor analysis, temperature dominated methane ignition above about 1100 K, while realistic H/OH radicals shortened ignition delay mainly in the 950–1100 K interval.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: HRM sensitivity maps varied initial temperature and radical concentration using states sampled from engine CFD.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Zero-dimensional chemistry isolates kinetics and omits turbulent transport.
evidence_candidates.potential_chapter_role: Thermal-versus-radical pathways in pilot-assisted NG ignition.

key_results: Reported radical effects shortened ID by up to about 4.5 CAD for H and 5.5 CAD for OH at 1400 RPM within the modeled range.
mechanisms: Pilot combustion supplies heat and reactive species; their relative influence depends on local temperature.
extraction_notes: Tier 2 targeted extraction; threshold retained as condition-specific qualitative output rather than universal property.

note_fields.Research Question: Does the main NG jet require a pilot trigger, and how do temperature and H/OH radicals affect ignition delay?
note_fields.Study Type and Configuration: CONVERGE engine CFD paired with Cantera homogeneous-reactor calculations at 1400 RPM/1285 Nm.
note_fields.Injection / Ambient Conditions: NG 234 bar and 328 K; pilot and gas timings/masses are tabulated in the paper.
note_fields.Main Physical Observations: NG-only CFD did not ignite; temperature and radicals both changed HRM ignition delay within bounded state ranges.
note_fields.Mechanism Proposed by Authors: Pilot combustion supplies the thermal/radical trigger; temperature dominates at sufficiently high initial temperature.
note_fields.Limitations: One operating point; sector CFD and zero-dimensional HRM introduce model dependence.
note_fields.Relevance to Review Mainline: Mechanistic bridge from pilot chemistry to main-jet ignition.

papers.tier1_role: Chapter-core numerical evidence on real-gas EoS effects in highly underexpanded hydrogen jets.
papers.study_context: Axisymmetric Favre-averaged multicomponent turbulent-jet computations with ideal, van der Waals, and Redlich–Kwong EoS.

cases.description: 75 MPa hydrogen issuing through a 0.3-mm inner-diameter nozzle into 5 MPa nitrogen.

source_locators.section: Real Gas Effects in Hydrogen Underexpanded Jets

parameters.definition: Hydrogen tank/injector total pressure.
Still-nitrogen ambient static pressure.
Nozzle inner diameter.
Computed jet mass flow with ideal-gas EoS.
Computed jet mass flow with Redlich–Kwong EoS.

process_relations.target_process: nozzle-exit state and downstream shock-cell thermodynamics
process_relations.notes: Jet topology persists but quantitative fields change.

mechanism_relations.notes: Largest differences occur in exit state.

mechanism_relations.target_node: centerline temperature, pressure, and Mach profiles
mechanism_relations.notes: Mach-disk geometry changes were smaller than field-profile changes.

evidence_candidates.claim: For the 75 MPa hydrogen-to-5 MPa nitrogen case, real-gas EoS changed computed nozzle-exit velocity and density by up to roughly 38% and 35%, and reduced mass flow by about 9–10% relative to the ideal-gas result.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Table 3 directly compares ideal, van der Waals, and Redlich–Kwong exit properties.
evidence_candidates.limitations: EoS comparison is numerical and tied to this high-pressure state/nozzle model.
evidence_candidates.potential_chapter_role: Real-gas modelling requirement for high-pressure gas injection.

evidence_candidates.claim: Real-gas modelling preserved the qualitative underexpanded-jet/Mach-disk structure but materially changed centerline thermodynamic and Mach-number profiles.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: The conclusion reports smaller geometry changes than the substantial downstream profile differences.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Axisymmetric RANS and classical cubic EoS choices.

key_results: Van der Waals and Redlich–Kwong mass flow were 10.1% and 8.7% below ideal; maximum downstream temperature, pressure, and Mach also changed materially.
mechanisms: EoS changes the isentropic nozzle-exit state, which propagates into shock-cell thermodynamics.
extraction_notes: Tier 2 targeted extraction; validation cases are summarized but not re-extracted as separate paper-local cases.

note_fields.Research Question: Is an ideal-gas EoS adequate for highly underexpanded high-pressure hydrogen injection?
note_fields.Study Type and Configuration: Axisymmetric turbulent multicomponent simulations validated against subsonic and underexpanded-jet experiments.
note_fields.Injection / Ambient Conditions: Hydrogen total pressure 75 MPa and 300 K into nitrogen at 5 MPa and 300 K through a 0.3-mm inner-diameter nozzle.
note_fields.Wave / Jet Structure: All EoS recovered barrel shock and Mach disk; geometry differences were smaller than thermodynamic/profile differences.
note_fields.Quantitative Results: Exit velocity/density differences reached roughly 38%/35%; real-gas mass flow was 8.7–10.1% below ideal.
note_fields.Mechanism Proposed by Authors: EoS-dependent nozzle expansion changes the exit state and downstream shock-cell fields.
note_fields.Limitations: Axisymmetric RANS and selected cubic EoS; not an engine-reacting case.
note_fields.Relevance to Review Mainline: Shows when high-pressure gas-jet structure is sensitive to real-gas property closure.

papers.study_context: Shock-tube experiments with actively generated parallel alcohol droplets and high-speed imaging.

Droplet liquid identified by the authors.

parameters.notes: Range compiled only from explicitly described cases.

parameters.definition: Adjacent-droplet spacing L divided by initial diameter D.
parameters.notes: Qualitative range retained; no inferred endpoints.

parameters.definition: rho_g*U_g^2*D/sigma using post-wave gas density/velocity and initial droplet diameter.
parameters.notes: Author-reported Weber number range and examples; no project recalculation.

parameters.definition: Author terminology for spacing- and Weber-dependent breakup modes.

dimensionless_definitions.notes: The complete author formula and scale definitions are preserved; component IDs are omitted because this record summarizes multiple experimental cases.

process_relations.target_process: bending direction, filament formation, and channel closure
process_relations.notes: Different effects dominate low- and high-We regimes.

mechanism_relations.notes: Low-We bending and high-We channel closure distinguished.

evidence_candidates.claim: At low Weber number, decreasing parallel-droplet spacing shifted breakup from bag toward trailing and shuttlecock modes through a spacing-dependent reversal of post-flattening bending.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: High-speed images and potential-flow pressure distributions support the mode boundary near L/D of order 2 for the tested geometry.
evidence_candidates.limitations: The theoretical analogue is two-dimensional cylinders; spherical-droplet boundary may shift.
evidence_candidates.potential_chapter_role: Parallel-droplet spacing effect at low Weber number.

evidence_candidates.claim: At higher Weber number, sufficiently small spacing promoted rapid equatorial filament formation and closure of the channel between adjacent droplets, producing a closed breakup mode.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: High-speed imaging distinguishes open and closed modes; smaller gaps close earlier and can reopen repeatedly.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Finite experimental parameter space and generated-droplet alignment variability.
evidence_candidates.potential_chapter_role: Collective breakup topology under shock-driven flow.

key_results: Low-We modes: bag, trailing, shuttlecock; high-We modes: open versus closed.
Smaller spacing accelerated filament formation and channel closure.
mechanisms: Gap-scale pressure and velocity redistribution changes bending at low We and equatorial shear/channel closure at high We.
extraction_notes: Tier 2 targeted extraction; phase-boundary curves were not digitized.

note_fields.Research Question: How do Weber number and spacing ratio govern shock-induced breakup of parallel-arranged droplets?
note_fields.Study Type and Configuration: Shock-tube experiment with actively controlled alcohol-droplet size/spacing and high-speed imaging, supported by potential-flow analysis.
note_fields.Droplet / Spray Initial Conditions: Parallel alcohol droplets with representative diameters 230–430 um; L/D varied broadly.
note_fields.Dimensionless Parameters: We uses post-wave gas density and velocity, initial D, and surface tension; the study spans O(10)–O(100).
note_fields.Main Physical Observations: Low-We spacing selects bag/trailing/shuttlecock modes; high-We spacing selects open/closed channel topology.
note_fields.Mechanism Proposed by Authors: Spacing redistributes gap pressure and equatorial velocity/shear, changing bending, filament formation, and channel closure.
note_fields.Limitations: Potential-flow model uses 2D cylinders; finite experimental regime and alignment variability.
note_fields.Relevance to Review Mainline: Direct multidroplet evidence that interaction spacing changes breakup mode under the same external forcing class.
